characters.continuity: Mortal Kombat series, original timeline (Mortal Kombat 1992 through Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance)
characters.summary: Liu Kang is a Shaolin martial artist and the champion of the first Mortal Kombat tournament. He fights with fast kicks (Bicycle Kick, Flying Kick) and fire projectiles, and can transform into a Chinese dragon. He is mortal: the Deadly Alliance of Shang Tsung and Quan Chi murdered him.

mechanisms: Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: Exposed while throwing some fireball techniques: open to low attacks and vulnerable if the first fireball is blocked (MK11 Low Dragon Fire)
mobility: Flies across the screen with the Bicycle Kick and Flying Kick
limitations: Mortal martial artist before his ascension; he was killed by Shang Tsung and Quan Chi

sources.supports: Fire projectiles, dragon transformation, Bicycle Kick and Flying Kick; champion after the first tournament; Shang Tsung is a nemesis he has defeated on numerous occasions; murdered by the Deadly Alliance of Shang Tsung and Quan Chi; MK11 fireball move openings.

feats.claim: Became champion after the first Mortal Kombat tournament.
feats.citation: Mortal Kombat (1992); Mortal Kombat Wiki, Liu Kang

notableResults.note: Shang Tsung is his nemesis, whom he has defeated on numerous occasions; the opened source does not detail each fight.

notableResults.opponent: Shang Tsung and Quan Chi (Deadly Alliance)
notableResults.note: Murdered at the Academy by the two sorcerers together; two-on-one.

campaignTags.claim: Commonly associated with fire, which he uses as fire projectiles.
Shoots fire projectiles (Fireball / Dragon Fire moves).

unknowns: Exact limits of his mortal stamina.
Defensive abilities (blocking, durability) are not described by the opened source.
Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Kang) was not opened in review; replaced by the Mortal Kombat Wiki page.

characters.summary: After Raiden merges his essence with Liu Kang's past and present selves, Liu Kang becomes a Fire God with Raiden's command of lightning and thunder, portal creation and flight. He defeats Kronika and becomes the new Keeper of Time; in Mortal Kombat 1 he watches over Earthrealm as God of Fire but abandons the Keeper's power after seeing it drove Kronika insane.

mechanisms: Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: Not established by the cited source
limitations: Abandoned the Keeper of Time's power after finding it drove Kronika insane (Mortal Kombat 1)
characters.formDifferences: Raiden's essence merged with Liu Kang's past and present selves makes him a Fire (and Thunder) God: he gains Raiden's lightning, portal creation and flight on top of his martial arts and fire, and becomes Keeper of Time.

sources.supports: Raiden merges his essence with Liu Kang, turning him into a Fire God; he inherits Raiden's command over lightning and thunder and the abilities to create portals and fly; becomes a Fire/Thunder God and defeats Kronika; new Keeper of Time; abandons the power after it drove Kronika insane.

notableResults.note: As Fire/Thunder God after merging with Raiden; won at the cost of the timeline.

campaignTags.claim: Raiden merging with him turns him into a Fire God.
Commands divine fire as the God of Fire.
Inherited Raiden's command over lightning and thunder.
Inherited Raiden's command over lightning and thunder.
Inherited Raiden's ability to create portals.

unknowns: Full extent of his control over time as Keeper of Time.
Defensive abilities and weaknesses of the god form are not described by the opened source.
Dragon summoning and a "temporal strike" technique were not found in the opened source and are not claimed.

characters.continuity: Super Mario series, Luigi's Mansion (GameCube) and the Super Smash Bros. moveset
characters.summary: Luigi is Mario's taller younger brother, a stronger jumper than Mario with notoriously low traction. In Luigi's Mansion he uses E. Gadd's Poltergust 3000 vacuum and a flashlight to stun and capture ghosts, rescues Mario from a painting and defeats King Boo. His Smash moveset adds a green Fireball, Green Missile, Super Jump Punch and Luigi Cyclone.

mechanisms: Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: Extremely low traction and slow aerial mobility (Smash Bros.)
limitations: The Poltergust needs a ghost stunned by the flashlight first, revealing its heart, before capture (Luigi's Mansion)

sources.supports: Smash moveset: green Fireball, Super Jump Punch, Luigi Cyclone, Green Missile; extremely low traction and slow airborne mobility; taller than Mario and jumps higher; Poltergust in later games.
Luigi uses E. Gadd's Poltergust 3000 and a flashlight to stun and capture ghosts, restores Mario from a painting and defeats King Boo, who fights him in a Bowser suit.
Luigi's listed moves include Green Missile, Ground Pound, Luigi Cyclone, Scuttle, Spin Jump and Triple Jump.

feats.claim: Restored Mario from a painting with the Ghost Portrificationizer after clearing the mansion with the Poltergust 3000.

notableResults.note: King Boo fought him from inside a Bowser suit; Luigi blasted the suit's head off and caught King Boo.

campaignTags.claim: Uses E. Gadd's inventions, the Poltergust 3000 and the Game Boy Horror, plus a flashlight.

unknowns: Cowardice as an exploitable weakness is not stated by the opened sources.
Hover jump is not listed by the opened sources.
Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luigi) was not opened in review; replaced by SmashWiki and Mario wiki pages.

characters.summary: Ice Luigi is the form Luigi takes after touching an Ice Flower in New Super Mario Bros. Wii. He shoots Ice Balls that trap normal enemies in blocks of ice.

mechanisms: Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: Not established by the cited source
limitations: Only normal enemies are said to be trapped in ice; the freeze is not described for bosses
characters.formDifferences: Touching an Ice Flower gives Luigi the power to shoot Ice Balls that freeze normal enemies into ice blocks.

sources.supports: Ice form (Ice Luigi redirects to Ice Mario) gives Mario, Luigi, Yellow Toad and Blue Toad in New Super Mario Bros. Wii the power to shoot Ice Balls; taken by touching an Ice Flower; normal enemies are trapped in ice blocks.

campaignTags.claim: Shoots Ice Balls that freeze enemies.
Ice Balls trap normal enemies in blocks of ice.

unknowns: How long the form lasts, and whether one hit removes it, is not stated in the opened source.
The bouncing arc and range of Ice Balls are not described in the opened source.

characters.summary: Grabbing a Super Star makes Luigi temporarily invincible: invulnerable to most enemies and obstacles and able to defeat most enemies by touching them, for only a few seconds.

mechanisms: Invulnerable to most enemies and obstacles while it lasts

weaknesses: Falling into a pit still costs a life
characters.formDifferences: A Super Star makes Luigi briefly invulnerable to most enemies and obstacles, lets him defeat most enemies on contact and, in New Super Mario Bros., makes him run faster.

sources.supports: Invincible form (Invincible Luigi redirects to Invincible Mario): invulnerable to most enemies and obstacles, defeats most by touch, lasts a few seconds, faster running in New Super Mario Bros., pits still cost a life; Mario and Luigi both turn invincible with a Super Star.

unknowns: Exact duration in seconds across games.
Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Mario) was not opened in review; replaced by the Mario wiki page.

characters.continuity: Street Fighter series (main games, Street Fighter II through Street Fighter V)
characters.summary: M. Bison, leader of Shadaloo, wields Psycho Power, an evil energy contrasted with Ryu and Ken's Hadou. He fights with the Psycho Crusher, Scissors Kick, Head Stomp and Knee Press Nightmare, teleports often and can hover. When a body fails he moves his essence into engineered or clone bodies.

mechanisms: Teleports to evade (Bison Warp-style dashes; Devil Reverse behind opponents)
Transfers his essence to a new body when the old one is destroyed

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
mobility: Psycho Crusher flies him at the opponent
limitations: The strain of Psycho Power was killing his body
Replacement bodies can be much weaker than the original

sources.supports: Psycho Power contrasted with Hadou; dying from the strain of Psycho Power; soul transferred into Rose's body; clone bodies; Akuma defeats/kills him in Super Street Fighter II Turbo; in SFV Charlie Nash's sacrifice weakens him, leaving Ryu to defeat him one last time.

Psycho Crusher, Scissors Kick, Head Stomp, Knee Press Nightmare; abilities to teleport and hover in the air; frequent teleporting; engineered replacement bodies, the new one much weaker; destroyed by Akuma with the Shun Goku Satsu.
SFV V-Trigger: dashes become Bison Warp-style teleports, Devil Reverse teleports behind opponents in mid-air, and Psycho Blast becomes stronger.

feats.claim: Survived the destruction of his body by transferring his essence into a body his scientists had engineered for that purpose.

notableResults.note: Charlie Nash's sacrifice weakened Bison first, leaving Ryu to defeat him.
Akuma kills him with the Shun Goku Satsu.

campaignTags.claim: Has the ability to teleport and makes frequent use of it.
Psycho Power lets him hover in the air.

unknowns: Exact number of spare clone bodies available at any time.
"Psychic" was not kept as a tag: the sources describe Psycho Power as an evil energy, not telepathy, telekinesis or mind control.
Psycho power barrier and high durability are not described by the opened sources.
The note that Ryu used the Power of Nothingness is not in the opened sources and was removed.

characters.continuity: Gears of War series (Gears of War to Gears of War 3)
characters.summary: Marcus Fenix is the leader of Delta Squad, a COG soldier who fights the Locust with a Lancer assault rifle and its chainsaw bayonet. With Dom Santiago he killed General RAAM aboard the Tyro Pillar, and in Gears of War 3 he held off Queen Myrrah while his father's Imulsion Countermeasure charged, then stabbed her to death.

techniques: Chainsaw bayonet melee (cuts through Locust hide)

mechanisms: Uses light (UV) and explosives against Kryll shields and swarms

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources (no superhuman durability is documented)
mobility: Not established by the cited sources
limitations: Conventional soldier who depends on his weapons and squad

sources.supports: Sgt. Fenix and Pvt. Santiago open fire on RAAM; Delta stays within the light; by interrupting RAAM's Kryll shield with UV light and explosives, Delta kills him.
Gears 3 ending: Delta engages Queen Myrrah while Adam's device charges; it activates and kills the Lambent instantly; Marcus stabs Myrrah to death after the Tempest's crash.
Lancer chainsaw bayonet cuts through Locust hide and more; Marcus' knife bayonet broke off, and he called for something that actually cuts.
Marcus Fenix is the leader of Delta Squad and a celebrated war hero.

feats.claim: Held off Queen Myrrah with Delta while his father's Imulsion Countermeasure charged; the device killed the Lambent instantly.

notableResults.note: With Dom Santiago and Delta; they broke RAAM's Kryll shield with UV light and explosives, then shot him.
She survived the Tempest's crash and Marcus stabbed her to death.

unknowns: "gadgets" tag removed: standard-issue military weapons and communications are not a gadget kit (owner ruling on standard-issue gear).
Armor type and protection are not described by the opened sources.
Roadie run, combat roll and active reload are gameplay mechanics not described by the opened sources.
Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcus_Fenix) was not opened in review; replaced by Gears of War Wiki and Prima pages.

characters.continuity: Super Mario series (platformers; final Bowser battle from Super Mario Odyssey)
characters.summary: Mario fights mainly by jumping (Jump, Spin Jump, Triple Jump, Long Jump, Ground Pound) and by power-ups. As Super Mario he can take a hit without losing a life, reverting to Small Mario. In Super Mario Odyssey he defeats Bowser in the final battle and captures him to escape the collapsing caverns.

mechanisms: Super Mario form absorbs a hit by reverting to Small Mario

weaknesses: Pits are lethal: a fall costs a life even while invincible
limitations: The Super Mario form only absorbs a hit; damage reverts him to Small Mario

sources.supports: Mario's listed moves include Jump, Double Jump, Triple Jump, Long Jump, Spin Jump, Ground Pound, Dash, Punch and Kick.
Super Mario (from a Super Mushroom) withstands a hit without losing a life, reverting to Small Mario.
Final battle of Super Mario Odyssey: Mario falls to the caverns and defeats Bowser for the final time, then captures the unconscious Bowser to clear the way out.
Even while invincible, Mario can still lose a life if he falls into a pit.

notableResults.note: Defeated him in the final battle, then captured the unconscious Bowser to escape.

unknowns: Full extent of his physical strength without power-ups.
Wall jumping is not in the opened move list.
The claim that he consistently defeats Bowser and rescues Peach across many games is not stated by the opened sources; only the Odyssey result is kept.
Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario) was not opened in review; replaced by Mario wiki pages.

weaknesses: Not established by the cited source
mobility: Briefly climbs or clings to walls and the Goal Pole
characters.formDifferences: A Super Bell gives Mario a cat suit: brief wall climbing and clinging, a claw swipe and a midair claw dive.

sources.supports: Cat Mario, introduced in Super Mario 3D World and obtained with a Super Bell, can briefly climb or cling to walls and the Goal Pole, claw-swipe enemies in front of him and claw-dive on enemies from midair.

unknowns: Whether one hit removes the suit is not stated in the opened part of the source.

mechanisms: Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: Reverts to Super Mario when he takes a hit (Super Mario Maker)
limitations: In most platformers only two fireballs can be in play at once
